text.p: Italian debt futures edged higher by late afternoon in largely a technical reaction helped by some support from the lira as the market awaits preliminary March CPI data from seven Italian cities, dealers said.

Comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan that the U.S. central bank should act pre-emptively against inflation caused many world bonds markets to fall on fears of a U.S. rate rise, but BTPs were one of the few to show gains.
Seven Italian cities will publish their preliminary CPI data for March around 1630 GMT today with many expecting the downward trend in inflation to continue.
Economists expect Italy's March CPI to fall to a year-on-year rate of 2.3 percent from 2.4 percent seen in February, while a monthly rise of 0.2 percent is seen for March from February's 0.1 percent.
Some strength from the lira against the mark was also helping to support BTP contracts today, dealers said.

On the domestic front, dealers said that the state's quarterly accounts are likely to be presented this week or early next, and these will give an indication of how large a mini-budget for 1997 will be needed.
